summary: Careful, well-documented preregistered paired experiment. Execution artifacts show a degenerate null outcome (600/600 validator passes in both arms) under shared_initial_candidate semantics; authors correctly interpret this as measuring validator/repair trigger behavior rather than generation-level improvements. Main remaining problems are bibliographic formatting and a concise Disclosure refinement; otherwise the study is reproducible, preregistered, and statistically straightforward.
critical_issues: References/bibliography are not presented as a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full bibliographic metadata. The manuscript lists cited_record_ids/DOIs but does not provide IEEE‑style reference entries that allow independent verification that each cited work supports the nearby claim.

Because the References are not presented in standard IEEE bibliographic form, the reviewer cannot verify that each in-text numeric citation maps to an actual bibliographic entry that supports the asserted claim.
required_revisions: Replace the current cited_record_ids/DOI list with a conventional IEEE numbered References section. Each reference entry must include full bibliographic metadata (authors, title, venue, year, and DOI/arXiv id where available). Ensure each numeric in-text citation [1],[2],... exactly corresponds to one IEEE reference entry.

Confirm in the manuscript (References or a short footnote) that every cited record actually supports the proximate claim. If a cited item supports only a weaker claim (e.g., 'proposed' or 'demonstrated in limited testbeds'), rephrase the manuscript claim to match the verified evidence.

Condense the Disclosure Statement so it remains concise (within the five pages) and does not duplicate execution logs or exhaustive provenance lists. Preserve the single required master_prompt locator and its SHA‑256 digest verbatim, and keep other provenance/hashing information exclusively in the archived artifacts rather than in main prose.

Explicitly ensure the Methods (not only the Disclosure) state that generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (the same sampled initial generation per pair was reused across baseline and guarded) and therefore that the confirmatory estimand measures validator/repair-trigger effectiveness rather than independent generation differences. (This point is present in several places but must appear clearly in Methods and in the Limitations paragraph.)

In Methods or an explicit short subsection, add a concise statement about runtime sampling fields: document that the archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset and explicitly note that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling (i.e., does not imply temperature=0). If sampling fields are archived, point readers to their exact artifact paths for reproduction.
optional_revisions: If available in the archived bundle, include the preregistered 'seeded 100-case validator‑audit' results (or a short summary) to quantify validator sensitivity/specificity; if not included in the manuscript text, add a concise pointer to the artifact path and hash in the Disclosure or Methods.

Add a brief, explicit discussion quantifying how the preregistered power/sample‑size assumptions (e.g., baseline ≈10%) were violated by the observed baseline rate (0%), and state the consequences for interpretation of H2 and minimal detectable effect in this execution.

If space permits, include a one‑paragraph operational recommendation (concrete checklist) for future generate→validate→repair evaluations (e.g., use independent per‑condition draws when measuring generation effects; run validator sensitivity audits; include adversarialized tasks).

Verify that all figure/table captions and the two tables referenced are present in the final five‑page PDF and that captions are succinct; if any referenced analysis artifacts (e.g., vendor‑stratified summaries) exist in the archive, optionally include a single small table or pointer to the artifact.
